The exponent of the product is psi(z_1, z_2) = psi_1(z_1) + psi_2(z_2), so Re and Im are additive; ask which of the known sufficient conditions for (H) is stable under that addition.", "obstruction": "The survey's weaker sufficient conditions (EKFR, C_log, C_log-log) are quantified over finite measures of finite 1-energy, with a measure-dependent sequence y_k. Under addition of exponents the level sets {y_k <= B(z) < y_k^beta} of B = 1 + Re(psi) change shape in the product space, and a measure on R^{n+m} of finite energy need not factor, so there is no way to produce the required sequence for the product from the two given sequences. That is exactly where the additivity argument stops.", "problem_id": "E0024", "recorded_at": "2026-09-08T12:11:24Z", "result": "Kanda-Forst is stable, which is what Proposition 3.10 uses, and so is Rao's strictly larger class, which the survey does not observe. Rao's condition is |Im(psi)| <= (1 + Re(psi)) f(1 + Re(psi)) with f increasing on [1, infinity) and the integral of 1/(lambda f(lambda)) divergent. If psi_1 and psi_2 both satisfy it with the same f, then using 1 + Re(psi_i) <= 1 + Re(psi) and monotonicity of f, |Im psi| <= |Im psi_1| + |Im psi_2| <= (2 + Re psi_1 + Re psi_2) f(1 + Re psi) <= 2 (1 + Re psi) f(1 + Re psi), so psi satisfies Rao's condition with f replaced by 2f, and the divergence of the integral of 1/(2 lambda f(lambda)) is unaffected. Resolvent densities pass to the product because a convolution with a density is a density. Hence: the answer to Question 4 is YES for every pair of processes in Rao's class. This is a genuine extension of Proposition 3.10 and it is easy; it is emphatically NOT an answer to the question as posed, because the survey's whole point (its Theorems 2.8, 2.11, 2.12) is that (H) holds for processes outside Rao's class.", "schema": "probability-attempt.v1", "substantive": true}

{"attempt_id": "E0026-A001", "author": "claude-prob1000-E-0908", "independent_check": "", "key_identity": "Splitting a Levy process at a jump scale writes it as an independent sum of a small-jump part and a compound Poisson part; the latter has bounded exponent and satisfies Kanda-Forst, and Rao's class is closed under independent sums, so only the small-jump part can obstruct (H).", "method": "Use the survey's own reduction (Question 7 implies Question 6, via Kesten's Theorem 1(f)) together with a stability observation for Rao's class.", "obstruction": "The reduction is only as good as Rao's condition, and the survey's own point is that (H) can hold outside it; conversely the infinite-variation hypothesis in Question 6 does not by itself force any lower bound on Re psi, so it does not force the ratio to be bounded. Getoor's conjecture, which subsumes this question, has been open for fifty years.", "problem_id": "E0026", "recorded_at": "2026-09-08T12:11:24Z", "result": "Combining the two gives a concrete class in which Question 6 has a positive answer. By the argument recorded in E0024, Rao's sufficient condition |Im psi| <= (1 + Re psi) f(1 + Re psi) with f increasing and the integral of 1/(lambda f(lambda)) divergent is stable under independent sums up to replacing f by 2f. Hence any one-dimensional Levy process that DECOMPOSES as an independent sum of processes each in Rao's class is itself in Rao's class and satisfies (H). Since a process with infinite jump variation can always be split at a scale into a small-jump part and a large-jump (compound Poisson) part, and compound Poisson processes have bounded exponent hence trivially satisfy Kanda-Forst, the question reduces to the SMALL-JUMP part alone: Question 6 holds whenever the small-jump component satisfies Rao's condition. That is a genuine reduction (the large-jump part is never the obstruction), and it is not an answer, since the small-jump part is exactly where an oscillating Levy density can break the ratio.", "schema": "probability-attempt.v1", "substantive": true}

{"attempt_id": "E0027-A001", "author": "claude-prob1000-E-0908", "independent_check": "", "key_identity": "For independent summands Re psi adds and |Im psi| is subadditive, so every sufficient condition for (H) of the pointwise form |Im psi| <= (1 + Re psi) f(1 + Re psi) with f increasing is closed under independent sums, up to replacing f by 2f.", "method": "Test each of the known sufficient conditions for (H) for stability under addition of the Levy-Khintchine exponents, since psi_{X+Y} = psi_X + psi_Y for independent summands.", "obstruction": "The survey's own weaker conditions (EKFR, C_log, C_log-log) are not of the pointwise form |Im psi| <= g(Re psi): they involve, for each finite measure of finite 1-energy, an integral over the level sets of B = 1 + Re psi against |Fourier transform of mu|^2 and a measure-dependent sequence y_k. Adding exponents moves those level sets, and no relation between the sequences for psi_X, psi_Y and one for psi is available. So the residual open case is exactly the pair where at least one summand satisfies (H) only through a measure-dependent condition.", "problem_id": "E0027", "recorded_at": "2026-09-08T12:11:24Z", "result": "Kanda-Forst is stable: if |Im psi_X| <= M(1 + Re psi_X) and |Im psi_Y| <= M(1 + Re psi_Y) then |Im psi| <= M(2 + Re psi_X + Re psi_Y) <= 2M(1 + Re psi). Rao's condition is also stable, with the same argument as in E0024: monotonicity of f and 1 + Re psi_i <= 1 + Re psi give |Im psi| <= 2(1 + Re psi) f(1 + Re psi), and the required divergence of the integral of 1/(lambda f(lambda)) is unaffected by the factor 2; the sum has resolvent densities as soon as one summand does. So the answer to Question 7 is YES whenever both summands lie in Rao's class - a class strictly larger than Kanda-Forst and containing all stable processes and every process with a nondegenerate Gaussian part. The survey does not record this. The caveat matters and is the reason this is not an answer: the survey's Theorems 2.8, 2.11 and 2.12 exist precisely because (H) holds for processes OUTSIDE Rao's class, and for those the argument gives nothing.", "schema": "probability-attempt.v1", "substantive": true}
